newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says rate decision "in due course".
newsitem.headline: Clarke says rate decision "in due course".

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said Bank of England Governor Eddie George would announce the result of today's monetary meeting in due course.
"Eddie will announce the decision in due course. That's the arrangement we have," he told Sky Television.

"The minutes will come out in due course and I'm sticking to my own rules...in order to avoid unsettlling the markets. Wait to see the minutes and then you'll see the sensible discussion which Eddie George and myself have had."
Minutes of monetary meetings are published six weeks afterwards.
Clarke said the disagreement between him and George at the December 11 meeting, minutes of which were published last week, had been over one quarter of one percent.

"We have low interest rates, we have the lowest mortgage rates for 30 years. Of course we have to set interest rates to ensure we keep the low inflation, our best inflation record for 50 years. which is why this recovery is so strong," he added.
George warned at the December 11 meeting that he might advise raising rates by half a percentage point to 6.50 percent in January or February.
But Clarke rejected his call for a quarter-point increase in December, arguing that the economic signals were mixed and the case had not been made for a tightening.
